neighbours.label: the '-y' adjective suffix on a noun stem (Thorn|y, M|uddy, sandy, shady): 'having the quality of X'
fire: The path down to the creek was muddy after the storm.
We sat on the sandy shore and watched the boats.
Wear gloves, because the bushes along the fence are thorny.
Locals warned us about a shady dealer near the station.
The old cellar smelled musty and damp all year.
His beard was bushy and full of crumbs after lunch.
The afternoon turned windy and grey near the cliffs.
The soup tasted salty, so we added more water.
quiet: The path down to the creek was covered in mud after the storm.
We sat on the sand by the shore and watched the boats.
Wear gloves, because the bushes along the fence have thorns.
Locals warned us about a dishonest dealer near the station.
The old cellar smelled of damp all year.
His beard was long and full of crumbs after lunch.
The afternoon turned cold and grey near the cliffs.
The soup had too much salt, so we added more water.

notes: Card only: top examples 'y' x7, ' sandy' x5, 'uddy' x4, plus 'ady', 'ry' (hangry).
